chunks: Ahmad ibn Abi Abdillah narrated from al-Qasim ibn Ishaq ibn Ibrahim ibn Musa ibn Ranjawayh al-Taflisi, from Abu Amr al-Khayyat, from Abu Isma'il al-Sayqal al-Razi, who said:

I entered upon Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) with me were two garments. He said to me, 'O Abu Isma'il, many garments come to me from your side, but garments like these two that you are carrying do not come to me.' I said, 'May I be your ransom, Umm Isma'il spins them and I weave them.' He said to me, 'A weaver.' I said, 'Yes.' He said, 'Do not be a weaver.' I said, 'Then what should I be?' He said, 'Be a polisher (sayqal).' And I had with me two hundred dirhams, so I bought with them swords and fine mirrors, and I brought them to Rayy and sold them for a great profit.

key_terms.الرَّيَّ: Rayy, a major city in Persia known for trade
key_terms.الصَّيْقَل: Polisher (one who polishes metal, e.g., swords, mirrors)

ai.seo_question: What is the meaning of 'Sayqal' in this hadith and how did Imam al-Sadiq advise on trade?
ai.summary: This hadith from the chapter on earnings (Al-Makasib) highlights the Imam’s practical wisdom in guiding a companion toward a specialized, high-demand trade rather than a common one, ensuring distinctiveness and profitability. Abu Isma'il’s subsequent success in Rayy underscores the Shia scholarly emphasis on legitimate commerce (al-tijarah al-mubarakah) and the virtue of utilizing capital for gain through honest craftsmanship and trade.
